facts.fact: Senegal's 2026 Digital Ministry budget was set at CFA 81.06bn, of which CFA 58.2bn (about 60%) goes to investment in digital and telecom projects; the document gives no date for the event, so its published date 2026-01 is used.
Budget tables: the budget for 2026 gives 31,915,316,171 XOF to 25 digital line(s). Dated by the budget document.

facts.fact: The Assembly finance committee adopted a 2025 budget of CFA 31.1bn for the digital sector of the Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital on 17 December 2024.
The digital sector's budget rose 93.2% from CFA 16.1bn in 2024 to CFA 31.1bn in 2025.
The whole ministry's budget rose 36.8% from CFA 42.7bn in 2024 to CFA 58.4bn in 2025.

The 2024 finance law (Loi 2023-18 of 15 December 2023) gave the digital economy sector of the Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital CFA 16.1bn, within a CFA 42.7bn ministry envelope.
The digital economy sector's budget rose 93.2% from CFA 16.1bn in 2024 to CFA 31.1bn in 2025, per committee reporting of 17 December 2024.
Budget tables: 8,600,000,000 XOF is published as actually spent on digital lines for 2025. Dated by the document that gives the figure.

facts.fact: Senegal's 2027 budget for the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Affairs is FCFA 64.97 billion in payment credits (about 99 million euros), as presented by minister Samba Diouf, with FCFA 14 billion for PAENS, 5.3 billion for Senegal Numerique SA and 475 million for the Startup Act; the plenary on it is blocked after the Assembly rejected the first part of the finance bill.
